Here's why this is the most effective approach: Direct Communication: Meeting with the distracted team member allows the project manager to directly address any concerns or feelings of exclusion, ensuring that the root cause of the distraction is understood and can be appropriately managed. Professionalism: This approach maintains professionalism by handling the issue discreetly, without involving the entire team or making assumptions about the motivations behind the distraction. Supportive Environment: It shows that the project manager cares about the well-being of all team members, fostering a supportive and inclusive team environment. Conflict Resolution: It provides an opportunity to resolve any potential conflict or misunderstanding in a private and constructive manner. Maintaining Focus: By addressing the distraction directly with the individual, the project manager can help the team member refocus on their work and improve their engagement in meetings. Overall, option B is a proactive and respectful way to handle the situation, ensuring that all team members feel heard and valued.

questions.q: In your project you need some assistance facilitating meetings, following up on action items, introducing new team members, and mediating conflicts. Who would be the most suitable team member type to assist you with those activities? *

o.t: Power Oriented team member.
Affiliate Oriented team member.
Achievement Oriented Team member.
Delivery Oriented Team member.

questions.e: The most suitable team member type to assist with facilitating meetings, following up on action items, introducing new team members, and mediating conflicts would be: B. Affiliate Oriented team member. Here's why: Facilitating Meetings: Affiliate-oriented team members excel at creating a cooperative and harmonious environment, which is crucial for effective meeting facilitation. Following Up on Action Items: These team members are often good at maintaining relationships and ensuring that commitments are met, making them effective at following up on action items. Introducing New Team Members: Their focus on building strong relationships and fostering a sense of belonging makes them ideal for welcoming and integrating new team members. Mediating Conflicts: Affiliate-oriented individuals are typically skilled in resolving conflicts and maintaining team cohesion, as they prioritize relationships and understanding different perspectives. Overall, an affiliate-oriented team member is well-suited to handle tasks that require strong interpersonal skills and a focus on team dynamics.

questions.q: A pharmaceutical project in the initiation phase is likely to be impacted by new market regulations. Which stakeholder categories should the project manager assign to the relevant regulatory body? *

o.t: External with high power/influence
Internal with high power/influence
Internal with antagonist/resistant support level
External with antagonist/resistant support level

questions.e: For a pharmaceutical project likely to be impacted by new market regulations, the relevant regulatory body should be assigned to: A. External with high power/influence Here's why: External: The regulatory body is not part of the organization but an external entity that imposes rules and regulations. High power/influence: Regulatory bodies have significant power and influence over the project because their regulations and approvals are critical to the project's success. This categorization ensures that the regulatory body's significant impact on the project is properly acknowledged and managed.

questions.q: What is the main goal of a Visionary leadership style? *

o.t: To support the team to self organise and decide a common vision.
To champion the adoption of the latest technologies and practices.
To provide long-term direction and engage the team to deliver it.
To prioritise and assign the tasks that are aligned with the vision.

questions.e: The main goal of a Visionary leadership style is: C. To provide long-term direction and engage the team to deliver it. Visionary leaders focus on setting a clear and inspiring vision for the future, providing direction, and motivating the team to work towards achieving that vision. They engage and align the team with the long-term goals of the project or organization.

questions.q: A new project manager is assigned to lead an agile project. The project manager wants to use motivation to encourage the team to perform well throughout the project. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Implement a reward system aimed to keep the team engaged and motivated.
Use the management reserves to fund some team-building activities.
Inflate project estimates to provide a financial buffer for team activities.
Ask project sponsor to fund more for team building activities.

questions.e: A. Implement a reward system aimed to keep the team engaged and motivated. Implementing a reward system is a proactive approach that directly targets team engagement and motivation, encouraging them to perform well throughout the project.

questions.q: A project team is working on a regulatory application that has a fixed duration for delivery. The team is using a hybrid approach and has divided development into three sprints. The first two sprints have not produced the required results mainly due to delays from functional units. The finance director is agitated due to the imminent sanctions if the application is not completed, and the project team is demoralized. Who is responsible for inspiring the project team? *

o.t: Product Owner
Financial Director
Functional Manager
Project Manager

questions.e: D. Project Manager The project manager is responsible for inspiring and motivating the project team. In this situation, they need to address the team's demoralization, manage the project's progress, and work to ensure that the team stays motivated despite the challenges and pressures.

questions.q: You are the project manager in an organization that is implementing agile delivery. You have experience as a scrum master and will perform this role in addition to the project management responsibilities. One of the team members wants to know what the main focus of a servant leader is. What will be your response? *

o.t: Client satisfaction and value delivered demonstration.
Growth and well-being of people and communities they belong to.
Stakeholders expectation management and communication.
Productivity and efficiency to achieve commitments made.

questions.e: B. Growth and well-being of people and communities they belong to. A servant leader focuses on the growth and well-being of their team members and the communities they are part of. This leadership style prioritizes serving others and supporting their development and needs, rather than focusing solely on tasks or outcomes.

questions.q: An expert resource avoids assignments that include working with a foreign contractor. How should the project manager resolve the situation? *

o.t: Question the expert privately about their reluctance or biases and insist on an inclusive attitude.
Issue a disciplinary warning to the expert and advise their functional manager to send them to diversity training.
Prevent delays and conflicts by hiring a consultant that the expert is willing to work with.
Reprimand the expert about their discriminatory behavior during a team meeting to set the right example.

questions.e: A. Question the expert privately about their reluctance or biases and insist on an inclusive attitude. Addressing the issue privately allows the project manager to understand the expert’s concerns or biases without creating a confrontational atmosphere. It provides an opportunity to discuss the importance of inclusivity and the expectation to work collaboratively with all team members, including foreign contractors. This approach promotes open communication and can help resolve the issue more effectively.

questions.q: After success in a particulary challenging project phase, a project manager reassigned a high-performing team member to a more strategic task. This is an example of what? *

o.t: Recognition
Risk acceptance
Mentorship
Scope change

questions.e: A. Recognition Reassigning a high-performing team member to a more strategic task after a successful project phase is a form of recognition. It acknowledges their valuable contributions and performance by providing them with more challenging and impactful opportunities, which can also motivate them and further enhance their career development.

questions.q: After an organization trained and implemented a new mandatory project management software application for all project staff, the project manager noticed that several team members show low levels of commitment to the new software. What is the cause for this? *

o.t: Fear of the unknown
Lack of required skills
Lack of clear project vision
Too much communication

questions.e: A. Fear of the unknown Low levels of commitment to a new software application often stem from a fear of the unknown. Team members may be apprehensive about adapting to new tools and processes, which can lead to resistance or lack of engagement. Addressing this fear by providing additional support, training, and clear communication can help increase commitment and ease the transition.

questions.q: Members from an agile team have been consistently tardy for stand-up meetings and are not meeting project target dates. The project leader assumes the issue may be difficulty with self-managing tasks within the team. What action should the project leader take? *

o.t: Aid the team to construct an agreement amongst them that details coveted behavioral norms.
Convene with the team to review the issues and detail actions to solve them.
Adopt a higher leadership role and set an example for the behavior needed.
Assemble agile and time management training for the team to complete.

questions.e: "Aid the team to construct an agreement amongst them that details coveted behavioral norms," focuses on creating a shared understanding and commitment within the team regarding expected behaviors and norms. Here's why this approach is effective: 1. Collective Ownership: Involvement: By involving the team in creating the agreement, everyone has a stake in the established norms. This collective ownership increases the likelihood that team members will adhere to the agreed-upon behaviors because they have had a role in defining them. 2. Clarity and Consensus: Defined Expectations: An agreement helps clarify what is expected in terms of punctuality, meeting deadlines, and other behaviors. When norms are clearly defined and agreed upon, there’s less room for misunderstandings or misinterpretations. 3. Accountability: Peer Influence: When team members agree on norms collectively, they are more likely to hold each other accountable. Peer pressure can be a powerful motivator for adhering to agreed behaviors. 4. Improved Morale: Empowerment: Engaging in the creation of norms can make team members feel valued and heard. This can lead to higher motivation and a sense of empowerment, which can improve their commitment to the project. 5. Sustainable Improvement: Long-Term Benefits: By constructing norms together, the team develops a stronger sense of unity and purpose, which can lead to more consistent and long-term improvements in behavior and performance compared to top-down mandates. In summary, option A leverages the team’s input to build a set of behavioral norms that everyone agrees to and commits to, fostering a collaborative environment where expectations are clear and accountability is shared.

questions.q: A project manager is working on a long-term project in a complex environment. The project manager's focus is on maintaining healthy team work and collaboration. What conflict resolution strategy should be used within the project team? *

o.t: Problem solving
Compromising
Accommodating
Consultation

questions.e: In a long-term project within a complex environment where the focus is on maintaining healthy teamwork and collaboration, the most suitable conflict resolution strategy is: A. Problem solving Reasons: Long-Term Focus: Sustainable Solutions: Problem solving seeks to address the root causes of conflicts rather than just treating symptoms. This approach is particularly important in long-term projects where ongoing issues can undermine team morale and productivity. Collaboration and Team Health: Engagement: Problem solving involves working collaboratively with team members to identify and resolve conflicts. This promotes a collaborative environment and helps in maintaining healthy teamwork. Root Cause Analysis: Thorough Resolution: By focusing on problem solving, the project manager can ensure that the underlying issues are addressed, leading to more effective and lasting solutions. This is crucial in complex environments where surface-level fixes may not be sufficient. Involvement of Team Members: Participation: Problem solving typically involves the participation of all parties involved in the conflict, ensuring that everyone’s perspectives are considered and that solutions are mutually agreed upon.

questions.q: Select three ways to improve and practice leadership skills. (Choose 3) *

o.t: Engage the team in the project process.
Be actively involved in the project tasks.
Treat each team member the same way.
Ask for feedback and analyze the results.
Use democracy for all team decisions.

questions.e: To improve and practice leadership skills, consider these three approaches: A. Engage the team in the project process. Rationale: Actively involving the team in the project process helps in building trust, ensuring buy-in, and enhancing collaboration. It allows leaders to understand team dynamics better and fosters a sense of ownership among team members. D. Ask for feedback and analyze the results. Rationale: Seeking feedback from team members and analyzing the results provides valuable insights into one’s leadership effectiveness. It helps identify areas for improvement and demonstrates a willingness to grow and adapt, which is crucial for effective leadership. B. Be actively involved in the project tasks. Rationale: Being actively involved in the project tasks shows commitment and helps leaders understand the challenges faced by their team. It also allows leaders to provide better guidance and support, leading by example and reinforcing their leadership presence.

questions.q: A project manager is not sure if the team has the critical skills needed to implement a key feature of an upcoming deliverable. In order to mitigate the risk of sprint failure, what should the project manager do? *

o.t: Ask for support from the sponsor to replace the low performers with new team members with a specific skill set.
Negotiate with the stakeholder to postpone this key feature to a later release while figuring out a better alternative.
Identify the potential skill gap and propose a strategy to address the gaps with training, mentoring, or coaching.
Embrace the risk, accept the sprint failure, and try to motivate the team toward better performance in the future.

questions.e: The best approach to mitigate the risk of sprint failure due to potential skill gaps is: C. Identify the potential skill gap and propose a strategy to address the gaps with training, mentoring, or coaching. Why This Approach? Proactive Skill Development: By identifying skill gaps and proposing strategies such as training, mentoring, or coaching, the project manager takes a proactive approach to address the issue. This helps ensure that the team develops the necessary skills to complete the key feature successfully. Long-Term Solution: Addressing the skill gaps with training and coaching provides a sustainable solution that benefits not just the current project but future projects as well. It builds the team's overall capability and confidence. Team Morale and Engagement: Investing in the team's development can improve morale and engagement, as team members often appreciate opportunities for growth and learning.

questions.q: A chief technology officer (CTO) is enthusiastic about an organization's recent adoption of servant leadership practices. The CTO requests that all project managers apply servant leadership practices, but seems to be unsure of the practical applications. Which statement below best represents how the project manager should respond to the CTO's request? *

o.t: Explain that servant leadership can be adapted and applied to any project situation.
Remind the CTO that servant leadership is more suited for projects using agile methods.
Clarify that servant leadership practices typically focus on the client's preferences.
Affirm that servant leadership only works for projects with substantial resources.

questions.e: The best response to the CTO's request for practical applications of servant leadership is: A. Explain that servant leadership can be adapted and applied to any project situation. Why This Response? Adaptability: Servant leadership is a flexible approach that can be adapted to various project environments, including those that are not necessarily agile. It focuses on serving the needs of the team and supporting their growth, which is valuable in any project context. Broad Application: Servant leadership is not limited to specific types of projects or methodologies. It emphasizes leadership qualities such as empathy, listening, and empowerment, which can positively impact team dynamics and project outcomes regardless of the project type. Alignment with Modern Leadership Practices: This response aligns with the current trend in leadership, where the focus is on supporting and developing team members, which is relevant to both traditional and agile project environments.

questions.q: What are the four team-building leadership styles? *

o.t: Visionary, affiliative, coaching and participative
Visionary, affiliative, coaching and pace setting
Visionary, affiliative, coaching and directive
Visionary, affiliative, coaching and high waters

questions.e: The four team-building leadership styles are: A. Visionary, affiliative, coaching and participative Explanation: Visionary: Provides a clear and compelling vision for the future, inspiring and guiding the team toward a shared goal. Affiliative: Focuses on creating harmony and emotional bonds within the team, promoting a positive work environment and strong relationships. Coaching: Develops team members by providing guidance, feedback, and support to enhance their skills and performance. Participative: Encourages team involvement in decision-making processes, fostering collaboration and leveraging the collective input of the team. These styles are designed to build effective and cohesive teams by addressing different aspects of team dynamics and individual development.

questions.q: A project manager is assigned to a mobile application development project. The project manager realizes that an agile approach is better suited for the project, but most of the team is not experienced in agile approaches. What should the project manager do next if the organization is open to using an agile approach? *

o.t: Request that the project be reassigned to a project team with agile experience.
Ask to replace the team members who have never used agile approaches.
Arrange training on agile principles and mindset for the existing project team.
Use a predictive approach since the project team is already familiar with that approach.

questions.e: The correct action for the project manager in this situation is: C. Arrange training on agile principles and mindset for the existing project team. Explanation: Arrange Training: Since the organization is open to using an agile approach, providing training on agile principles and mindset will help the existing team understand and adopt agile practices. This investment in upskilling the team supports their development and aligns their work with the new approach, improving their effectiveness in delivering the project. Request Reassignment or Replacement: Reassigning the project or replacing team members might be extreme measures and could disrupt project continuity and team dynamics. Using a Predictive Approach: Although using a predictive approach might seem easier with the current team's familiarity, it would not align with the organization's openness to agile and could lead to missed opportunities for improving project outcomes through agile practices.

questions.q: The project manager of an AI project leads with grace and confidence. They provide support, listen attentively, and allow their team members to work under little supervision. What model of worker behavior does the project manager exhibit? *

o.t: Expectancy theory
Theory X
Theory Y
Theory Z

questions.e: The project manager exhibits: C. Theory Y Explanation: Theory Y: This theory, developed by Douglas McGregor, assumes that employees are self-motivated, enjoy taking responsibility, and are capable of self-direction. The project manager's approach of providing support, listening attentively, and allowing team members to work with little supervision aligns with Theory Y's view of trusting and empowering employees to achieve their best performance. Theory X: This theory assumes that employees are inherently lazy and need to be closely supervised and controlled. The project manager's style does not fit this model. Expectancy Theory: This theory, proposed by Victor Vroom, focuses on the relationship between effort, performance, and rewards. It is more about how individuals expect their efforts to lead to performance and rewards, rather than a leadership style. Theory Z: Developed by William Ouchi, Theory Z emphasizes long-term employment, collective decision-making, and individual responsibility, but it does not specifically describe the leadership style as presented.

questions.q: A sales manager is overpromising deliverables beyond the contractual scope. In order to resolve the disagreement, the project manager wishes to find someone with a higher ranking in the sales department who is favorable to the project. What project data should the project manager consult? *

o.t: Stakeholder power/interest grid
Communications management plan
Resource breakdown structure
Organizational process assets

questions.e: The project manager should consult: A. Stakeholder power/interest grid Explanation: Stakeholder power/interest grid: This tool helps in identifying and analyzing stakeholders based on their level of power and interest in the project. By consulting this grid, the project manager can find someone with a higher ranking in the sales department who has a favorable stance towards the project, which is crucial for resolving the disagreement and addressing the overpromising issue. Communications management plan: This plan outlines how communication will be handled throughout the project, but it does not specifically help in identifying influential stakeholders or resolving conflicts. Resource breakdown structure: This document shows the breakdown of project resources but does not address stakeholder influence or help in resolving conflicts related to overpromising. Organizational process assets: These are assets from previous projects or organizational knowledge that may assist in project management, but they do not specifically help in identifying influential stakeholders for conflict resolution.

questions.q: An internal project has delivered its scope on time, within budget, and with the expected quality. The client was satisfied with the result and it enabled them to launch the new product to market. However, the product did not attract the expected interest and did not cover the investment made. The project team is aware of these results and it is impacting their morale to deliver the next project. How should the project manager handle this situation? Choose 2 answers. *

o.t: Have a discussion with the team to explain that the product success is not a direct result of the project and it does not reflect their performance
Have a meeting with the business to make sure they understand the project met its objectives
No action is necessary, as the project manager is only responsible for the project deliverables.
Have a conversation with the business sponsor to validate the strategy for the new project based on this result.

questions.e: In this situation, the project manager should: A. Have a discussion with the team to explain that the product success is not a direct result of the project and it does not reflect their performance. D. Have a conversation with the business sponsor to validate the strategy for the new project based on this result. Explanation: A. Have a discussion with the team to explain that the product success is not a direct result of the project and it does not reflect their performance. This is important to address the team's morale. By clarifying that the project met its objectives and that the product’s market performance is not a direct reflection of the team's efforts, the project manager can help maintain the team's motivation and focus on future projects. D. Have a conversation with the business sponsor to validate the strategy for the new project based on this result. This ensures that lessons learned from the current project's market performance are taken into account when planning the next project. It helps in refining strategies to better align with market expectations and avoid similar issues in the future.

questions.q: A functional manager questions whether certain aspects of a project are in compliance with the project's goals. Which document should the project manager review to address the functional manager's concern? *

o.t: Statement of work (SOW)
Project charter
Project management plan
Project management information system (PMIS)

questions.e: B. Project charter The project charter is the right document for this situation because it outlines the project's objectives, goals, and overall scope. It serves as a reference point to ensure that all project activities align with the intended purpose and goals of the project. If the functional manager has concerns about compliance with project goals, the project charter will provide clarity on whether the current aspects of the project align with the originally defined goals and objectives.

questions.q: A project manager is leading a hybrid project. Several team members recently exited the project, including the only individual with a specific critical skill. At the beginning of a new sprint, the project manager identifies a task requiring this missing skill. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Rescope the project to remove the task requiring the missing skill.
Assess the impact of the missing skill on the project.
Postpone the task until a replacement is recruited.
Reassign the task to another project team with the necessary skills.

questions.e: In this situation, the project manager should: B. Assess the impact of the missing skill on the project. Explanation: Assessing the Impact: Before taking any action, it's crucial to understand how the absence of the critical skill affects the project. This assessment will help determine the severity of the issue and the possible implications for the project timeline, scope, and deliverables. Options Based on Assessment: Rescoping the Project: If the assessment reveals that the missing skill is crucial and cannot be replaced or learned quickly, then rescoping might be necessary. Postponing the Task: If the skill can be acquired or the task can be postponed without severely impacting the project, this might be a viable option. Reassigning the Task: If there's another team with the necessary skill or if you can quickly recruit someone with the skill, reassigning the task might work. Assessing the impact allows for informed decision-making and helps in choosing the most appropriate response based on the project's needs and constraints.

questions.q: Which leadership behavior is least likely to boost motivation in an Agile project team? *

o.t: Instruct the team to immediately use a new productivity tool.
Ask the team to vote if a new work method should be adopted.
Assign individual team members to the tasks in the backlog.
Ask for a volunteer to run a customer satisfaction survey.

questions.e: In Agile projects, motivation is often driven by team autonomy and involvement in decision-making. A. Instructing the team to immediately use a new productivity tool might not boost motivation because it takes away the team's autonomy and doesn't involve them in the decision-making process. This top-down approach can lead to resistance or disengagement, as it doesn't consider the team's input or buy-in. In contrast: B. Asking the team to vote on a new work method involves them in decision-making, which can increase motivation. C. Assigning tasks in the backlog might be necessary but doesn't inherently impact motivation unless done thoughtfully. D. Asking for a volunteer to run a customer satisfaction survey allows team members to take on roles voluntarily, which can be motivating. By involving the team in decisions and giving them choices, you’re more likely to foster a motivated and engaged team.

questions.q: A project manager wants to establish an incentive and rewards strategy for the project team. What approach should be taken? *

o.t: Ask Human Resources department which incentives should be provided.
Check on budget availability in order to determine specific reward amounts.
Provide an opportunity for publicly presenting the outcomes.
Identify the specific needs for each team member to determine incentives.

questions.e: The best approach for establishing an incentive and rewards strategy is: D. Identify the specific needs for each team member to determine incentives. Here’s why: Personalization: Different team members are motivated by different things. By identifying individual needs and preferences, the project manager can tailor incentives to what will be most meaningful and motivating for each person. Effectiveness: Understanding what each team member values ensures that the incentives are effective and aligned with their personal motivations, leading to better overall engagement and performance. Equity: This approach helps ensure that incentives are fair and appropriate, addressing the diverse motivations within the team.

questions.q: At the midway point of a project, the project manager was informed of a market movement that would make the project results useless to the client. This information could cause the project to be cancelled or at least a big change on the scope and desired outcome. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Prepare all status reports and demos to keep the client focused on the project execution that has been successful.
Have a transparent discussion with the project sponsor, offering support on the strategy evaluation if needed.
Continue working on the project execution, as the business strategy is not responsibility of the project manager.
Halt the project immediately, as the project manager knows it will be useless to the client.

questions.e: The most appropriate action for the project manager is: B. Have a transparent discussion with the project sponsor, offering support on the strategy evaluation if needed. Here’s why: Transparency and Communication: It's crucial to communicate the potential impact of market changes to the project sponsor. The sponsor needs to be aware of the situation to make informed decisions about the project's future. Collaboration: Offering support on strategy evaluation shows that the project manager is proactive and committed to finding a solution, rather than just continuing or halting the project without considering the broader context. Alignment: The project manager's role includes ensuring that the project aligns with the client's needs and market conditions. This approach helps in reassessing the project's relevance and making necessary adjustments or decisions about its continuation.

questions.q: At which stage in the Tuckman team development model should the project manager put the most focus on increasing team motivation? *

o.t: Forming
Storming
Norming
Performing

questions.e: In the Tuckman team development model, the project manager should put the most focus on increasing team motivation during the A. Forming. Here’s why: In the Forming stage of the Tuckman team development model, the team is in its initial phase of coming together. During this stage, team members are just beginning to understand their roles, the project's objectives, and how they will work together. Here’s why the project manager should focus on increasing team motivation during this stage: Characteristics of the Forming Stage: Uncertainty and Ambiguity: Team members are unsure about their roles and how they fit into the team. This uncertainty can lead to hesitation and a lack of confidence. Building Relationships: Members are getting to know each other and establishing working relationships. This is a time for establishing norms and understanding group dynamics. Initial Impressions: This stage sets the tone for how the team will function. Positive experiences and early successes can build a foundation for trust and collaboration. Why Focus on Motivation: Encourage Engagement: Motivating team members early on helps them become more engaged and committed to the team's goals. When people feel valued and understood, they are more likely to contribute actively and positively. Build Trust and Relationships: Motivated team members are more likely to be open, share information, and build strong working relationships. This can help in overcoming initial barriers and fostering a collaborative environment. Establish Positive Norms: Early motivation helps in setting positive team norms and expectations. When team members see enthusiasm and commitment from the project manager, it can encourage them to mirror those behaviors. Reduce Anxiety: Addressing motivational needs can help alleviate anxiety and uncertainties that team members may feel. This can lead to a more cohesive and effective team as they move into the Storming stage and beyond. By focusing on motivation during the Forming stage, the project manager can help the team navigate this initial phase more smoothly and set a strong foundation for future stages of team development.

questions.q: A project manager leads two teams who typically work on three or four concurrent short projects. The teams are motivated and comply with Six Sigma practices. Which type of waste will most likely occur in this situation? *

o.t: Defects
Time wasting
Partially done work
Task switching

questions.e: In the described situation where a project manager leads two teams working on multiple concurrent short projects, the type of waste most likely to occur is: D. Task switching Why Task Switching is Likely: Concurrent Projects: With multiple short projects running concurrently, team members may frequently switch between different tasks or projects. This can lead to inefficiencies as they need to refocus and reorient themselves for each new task. Context Switching Costs: Each time team members switch from one task to another, there is a cost associated with the time and effort required to re-engage with the new task. This can reduce overall productivity and increase the time needed to complete tasks. Loss of Focus: Frequent task switching can lead to a loss of focus and lower quality of work, as team members may struggle to maintain the same level of concentration on each task. Other Types of Waste: A. Defects: This refers to errors or quality issues in the work produced. While defects can occur, they are not the primary concern given the context of task switching. B. Time Wasting: While time wasting can occur, the primary concern in this scenario is the inefficiency related to task switching rather than intentional or incidental time waste. C. Partially Done Work: This refers to work that is not completed or is incomplete. It might be a concern, but in this scenario, task switching is a more direct issue given the nature of managing multiple projects. Thus, task switching is the most likely type of waste to occur in a situation with multiple concurrent short projects and motivated teams.

questions.q: Which statement correctly differentiates management from leadership? *

o.t: Managers ask how and when; leaders ask what and why.
Managers focus on long-term goals; leaders focus on short-term goals.
Managers challenge the status quo; leaders accept the status quo.
Managers inspire trust; leaders rely on control.

questions.e: The correct statement that differentiates management from leadership is: A. Managers ask how and when; leaders ask what and why. Explanation: Managers typically focus on the execution of processes and tasks. They are concerned with the details of how tasks are completed and when they are to be done. Their role often involves organizing resources, planning, and ensuring that projects adhere to established processes and timelines. Leaders, on the other hand, focus on the broader vision and purpose. They ask what needs to be done and why it is important. Leaders are more concerned with inspiring and guiding teams towards a shared vision and understanding the underlying reasons behind goals and objectives.

questions.q: A hybrid project has the following characteristics: It is in the early stages. It has a brand new team. The project manager will be very busy executing other projects during the first two weeks of the project. During this early stage, how should the project manager develop the new project team? *

o.t: Ensure the team understands self-organizing principles.
Plan and host several team-building events to normalize the team.
Provide daily project status updates to keep the team informed.
Get to know each team member through one-on-one conversations.

questions.e: In the context of early-stage projects, especially with new teams and a project manager who will be occupied with other responsibilities, ensuring that the team understands self-organizing principles is crucial. Here’s why: 1. Building Autonomy: Self-organizing principles empower teams to make decisions and manage their work independently. This is particularly important when the project manager is not available to provide constant oversight. By understanding these principles, the team can take ownership of their tasks and responsibilities, reducing the need for micromanagement. 2. Encouraging Collaboration: A self-organizing team tends to be more collaborative and proactive. When team members understand how to self-organize, they are more likely to communicate effectively, resolve issues on their own, and support each other. This is crucial for maintaining progress and addressing challenges, especially when the project manager is busy with other projects. 3. Fostering a Positive Work Environment: Self-organizing principles encourage team members to take initiative and contribute to decision-making. This fosters a positive and inclusive work environment where team members feel valued and motivated. It can also lead to higher job satisfaction and better performance. 4. Reducing Dependency on the Project Manager: By focusing on self-organizing principles, the project manager helps the team become less reliant on their direct supervision. This is beneficial when the project manager is occupied with other tasks, as the team can continue to function effectively without needing constant guidance. 5. Enhancing Flexibility and Adaptability: Self-organizing teams are generally more adaptable to changes and challenges. They are used to making adjustments and finding solutions on their own, which is essential in a dynamic project environment. In summary, ensuring that a new project team understands and adopts self-organizing principles helps establish a foundation for autonomy, collaboration, and effective performance. This approach is particularly valuable when the project manager is juggling multiple responsibilities and needs the team to be capable of operating independently.

questions.q: A project team has successfully completed a project. The same team and three new people start another project led by a new scrum master. How will the new scrum master lead? *

o.t: High directive, high supportive
Low directive, high supportive
High directive, low supportive
Low directive, low supportive

questions.e: In this scenario, the new Scrum Master will need to balance their approach to leadership, considering that the team has experience but includes new members and is being led by a new Scrum Master. The most appropriate leadership style for a new Scrum Master in this context would be: B. Low directive, high supportive Here’s why: 1. Team Experience: The team has successfully completed a project and has experience, which means they likely have a good understanding of Agile practices and team dynamics. The new Scrum Master doesn’t need to be highly directive since the team already has experience and knowledge. 2. Integration of New Members: With the addition of new team members, the Scrum Master will need to focus on integrating these new members effectively. High support is crucial to help the new members adapt to the team and understand the project’s goals and processes. 3. Building Trust and Relationships: A high supportive approach helps in building trust and rapport with the existing team and new members. It’s important for the Scrum Master to support the team, address concerns, and foster a collaborative environment, especially when establishing their leadership. 4. Encouraging Self-Organization: The Scrum Master should encourage the team to self-organize and take ownership of their work. A low directive approach supports this by allowing the team to operate with a degree of autonomy while still providing guidance and support as needed. In summary, a low directive, high supportive approach helps the new Scrum Master support the existing experienced team and effectively integrate new team members, fostering a collaborative and supportive environment.

questions.q: A project is in the implementation phase. A new project manager discovers that the team members have no previous experience with the technology used for the project. However, there are several functional managers that have experience with the technology. What should the project manager do first to ensure the successful performance of the team? *

o.t: Ask functional managers to act as mentors or coaches for the team.
Request that the sponsor substitute experienced team members.
Identify the risks associated with team members' inexperience.
Develop status reports to monitor the team's skills and competencies.

questions.e: In this situation, the project manager should take the following action to ensure the successful performance of the team: A. Ask functional managers to act as mentors or coaches for the team. Here’s why: 1. Utilize Available Expertise: Functional managers have experience with the technology and can provide valuable guidance and support to the team. By involving them as mentors or coaches, the project manager can leverage their expertise to help the team get up to speed more quickly and effectively. 2. Address Inexperience Directly: The team’s lack of experience with the technology is a significant issue that needs to be addressed. Mentoring and coaching from experienced functional managers will help bridge the gap in knowledge and skills. 3. Enhance Team Performance: Mentoring and coaching can accelerate the learning process for the team members, improving their performance and increasing their confidence in using the technology. This support is crucial for the successful implementation of the project. 4. Foster Collaboration: Involving functional managers as mentors promotes collaboration between different parts of the organization, ensuring that the team receives the support and expertise needed to overcome their initial inexperience.

questions.q: In the company cafeteria, a project manager overhears an unengaged stakeholder mocking the style of language used in the project manager's status report. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Meet with the stakeholder privately to find out how to make communication more engaging.
Ask the company's public relations officer for tips on how to make written communications more captivating.
Stop sending the status reports to the stakeholder and use only direct email to communicate with them.
Update the project social contract to prohibit disrespectful communications when referring to project members.

questions.e: In this situation, the project manager should: A. Meet with the stakeholder privately to find out how to make communication more engaging. Here’s why: 1. Address Concerns Directly: Meeting privately allows the project manager to address the stakeholder's concerns and feedback directly. This can help clarify any misunderstandings and provide an opportunity to improve communication methods. 2. Improve Communication: By understanding the stakeholder’s perspective, the project manager can adjust the communication style to better meet the stakeholder’s needs and preferences, making the reports more engaging and effective. 3. Maintain Professionalism: Handling the issue privately maintains professionalism and avoids escalating the situation. It shows a willingness to listen and adapt, which can foster a better working relationship with the stakeholder. 4. Avoid Unnecessary Escalations: B. Asking the public relations officer might be useful for general tips, but it doesn’t address the specific feedback or build a relationship with the stakeholder. C. Stopping the status reports could lead to a lack of transparency and might not resolve the underlying issue. D. Updating the project social contract could be seen as a punitive measure and might not address the specific feedback from the stakeholder. In summary, meeting with the stakeholder privately to discuss their feedback and find ways to improve communication is the most constructive approach. It shows responsiveness and a commitment to effective stakeholder engagement.

questions.q: After preparing the project management plan, a project manager schedules a meeting with key stakeholders to finalize the planning phase. The project manager is now preparing for the executing phase. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Define the project and create the project charter.
Put the project plan into action.
Ensure all deliverables are completed.
Address risks to make sure the project is on track.

questions.e: After preparing the project management plan and scheduling a meeting with key stakeholders to finalize the planning phase, the next step for the project manager is: B. Put the project plan into action. Here’s why: 1. Transition to Execution: Once the project management plan is finalized and approved, the next logical step is to implement it. This involves moving from the planning phase to the executing phase, where the project team begins working on the tasks and activities outlined in the plan. 2. Implementation of Strategies: Putting the plan into action means starting the actual work as per the strategies and schedules defined in the project management plan. It’s crucial to transition smoothly to execution to ensure that the project goals are met. 3. Project Monitoring and Control: Once execution begins, the project manager will also need to focus on monitoring progress, addressing any issues, and ensuring that the project stays on track. However, the immediate next step is to start executing the plan.

questions.q: A new project manager is hired to replace a project manager who was recently transferred to another project. The team members tell the new project manager that the project is behind schedule due to delays in document approvals from the customer. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Meet with the customer to discuss the delays and negotiate a new deadline.
Talk to the previous project manager to understand the situation better.
Reach out to the customer and request expedited document approvals.
Assess the impact of the delays on the project schedule and budget.

questions.e: Option B, “Talk to the previous project manager to understand the situation better,” involves seeking insights from the individual who was previously managing the project. Here’s why this approach is beneficial: Context and History: The previous project manager has firsthand knowledge of the project’s history, including any ongoing issues with document approvals. Understanding past challenges and the context behind them can help the new project manager address the problem more effectively. Relationship Insight: The previous project manager may have insights into the relationship dynamics with the customer, including any specific preferences or concerns they might have. This can help the new project manager approach the situation with a better understanding of how to communicate and negotiate. Decision-Making: With detailed information about the nature and frequency of the delays, as well as any previous attempts to resolve them, the new project manager can make more informed decisions about how to address the issue and mitigate its impact on the project. Continuity: This approach ensures continuity in project management by leveraging the knowledge of the outgoing project manager, which can help in maintaining a smoother transition and avoiding potential pitfalls. By understanding the situation from the previous project manager's perspective, the new project manager can gain valuable insights that will aid in addressing the delays effectively and managing stakeholder expectations.

questions.q: A project manager recently joined an organization that is implementing a portfolio of strategic initiatives aimed at enhancing profitability. The project manager reviews a past project's business case with the project sponsor to ensure that the project was aligned with the organization's goals and to learn from its successes and failures. Which of the following project outcomes would be considered most successful in the context of this organization's strategic initiatives? *

o.t: The project was delivered under budget by 25%, and the overall duration was 20% longer than initially scheduled.
The project was delivered on budget, and the project management office (PMO) approved the project closure.
The project was delivered early, entered the market before the competition, and exceeded the budget by 10%.
The project was delivered on schedule, within budget, and yielded a 5% increase in projected product sales.

questions.e: In the context of the organization’s strategic initiatives aimed at enhancing profitability, the most successful project outcome would be: D. The project was delivered on schedule, within budget, and yielded a 5% increase in projected product sales. Here’s why this option represents the most successful outcome: Alignment with Strategic Goals: The project yielded a 5% increase in projected product sales, which directly contributes to the organization’s goal of enhancing profitability. This outcome aligns well with the strategic objective of increasing profitability. On-Schedule Delivery: Delivering the project on schedule is crucial for meeting market demands and achieving timely benefits, which is essential in a competitive environment. On-Budget Delivery: Staying within budget is important for maintaining financial health and maximizing return on investment. It ensures that the project’s financial resources were managed effectively. Measurable Benefit: The increase in projected product sales is a tangible and measurable benefit that directly impacts profitability, making it a clear indicator of project success in terms of strategic value. Options A, B, and C, while they may have some positive aspects, do not demonstrate as clear a link to strategic objectives or have certain drawbacks: A: Delivered under budget but with a longer duration; the delay could affect market opportunities and profitability. B: On budget and PMO-approved but lacks a specific impact on strategic goals or profitability. C: Early delivery and market entry are positive, but exceeding the budget undermines the cost-efficiency aspect.

questions.q: A project manager is assigned to a project that will ensure that the organization meets regulatory compliance with new legislation. In which phase of the project should the project manager document compliance objectives? *

o.t: Initiation phase
Planning phase
Execution phase
Closing phase

questions.e: The correct answer is A. Initiation phase. During the Initiation phase, the project manager identifies and documents key project objectives, including compliance objectives, to ensure the project aligns with organizational and regulatory requirements from the start. This helps in setting a clear scope and direction for the project, ensuring that all necessary compliance aspects are considered early on.

questions.q: A project manager is assigned to a long-term project with a duration of three years. Which approach should the project manager take to address near-term activities, while long-term work is planned at a high level and detailed later? *

o.t: Focus on acquiring a team and deliver as soon as possible.
Engage the sponsor in the validation and prioritization processes.
Perform workshops with the client for delivery dates.
Validate the requirements and perform rolling wave planning.

questions.e: For a long-term project with a duration of three years, the most effective approach to address near-term activities while planning long-term work at a high level and detailing it later is: D. Validate the requirements and perform rolling wave planning. Explanation: Rolling wave planning is a technique used in project management to plan the project in waves or phases. Initially, the project is planned at a high level, focusing on near-term activities and deliverables. As the project progresses and more information becomes available, detailed planning is carried out for the upcoming phases. This approach is particularly useful for long-term projects where the complete scope and requirements may evolve over time. Validating requirements ensures that the near-term activities are based on accurate and agreed-upon requirements, which helps in creating a solid foundation for the detailed planning of future phases.

questions.q: A project manager is leading a team on a new development project. The team is made up of a diverse group of people with different personalities and work styles. The project manager is committed to creating a cohesive and productive team, so they decided to introduce the DISC behavior model to help team members understand each other better. Based on the DISC behavior model, which of the following characteristics best describes the Influence style? *

o.t: Direct, result-oriented, and firm
Outgoing, enthusiastic, optimistic
Accommodating, patient, humble, tactful
Analytical, reserved, and precise

questions.e: Based on the DISC behavior model, the characteristics that best describe the Influence style are: B. Outgoing, enthusiastic, optimistic Explanation: The Influence style in the DISC model is characterized by being outgoing, enthusiastic, and optimistic. Individuals with this style are often people-oriented, persuasive, and energetic. They focus on influencing others, fostering positive relationships, and creating a motivating environment.

questions.q: A project manager notices that a project is not running well and deliverables are falling behind. What is the first step the project manager should take in order to make a decision on how to progress with the project? *

o.t: Identify the problem.
Brainstorm solutions.
Establish a measurement criteria.
Set a goal.

questions.e: The first step the project manager should take in order to make a decision on how to progress with the project is: A. Identify the problem. Explanation: Identify the problem is the crucial first step because understanding the nature and scope of the issues affecting the project is essential for developing effective solutions. Once the problem is identified, the project manager can proceed with analyzing it, establishing measurement criteria, and brainstorming solutions to address the issues and get the project back on track.

questions.q: A project manager is overseeing the development and launch of a new product. In order to comply with the Project Management Office (PMO)'s guidelines, the project manager is required to ensure a Benefits Realization Plan outlining the business value to be delivered is created. The project manager is currently documenting the Roles and Responsibilities for this task in the form of a RACI chart. Who will be accountable for ensuring the project brings value to the organization? *

o.t: Project sponsor
Project manager
Solution architect
Steering committee

questions.e: In the context of ensuring that the project brings value to the organization, the person who will be accountable is: A. Project sponsor Explanation: The Project Sponsor is responsible for ensuring that the project aligns with the organization's strategic goals and delivers the anticipated benefits and value. They provide the necessary support and resources for the project and are ultimately accountable for the successful realization of the project's benefits. The project manager, while crucial in managing the project, typically handles the day-to-day operations and ensures the project meets its objectives, but the sponsor is accountable for the overall value and benefits realization.

questions.q: A​ product team is using a prototyping approach to deliver a multiyear business initiative. The project manager notices that a few user stories are taking longer to be delivered. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Review the project timeline and reallocate resources.
Conduct a retrospective with the team to identify bottlenecks.
Escalate the issue to senior management for intervention.
Modify the project scope to remove the delayed user stories.

questions.e: When a few user stories are taking longer to be delivered in a prototyping approach, the project manager should: B. Conduct a retrospective with the team to identify bottlenecks. Explanation: Conducting a retrospective allows the team to reflect on what is working well and what is causing delays. It helps in identifying specific issues, bottlenecks, or obstacles that might be impacting the delivery of user stories. This approach promotes a collaborative problem-solving environment and enables the team to implement improvements to enhance performance and address the delays effectively.

questions.q: A project is in the planning phase and requires tremendous time and effort for data collection and analysis. The project sponsor asks the project manager to skip a planned focus group discussion and brainstorming sessions in an effort to accelerate the process. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Report the issue to the project steering committee.
Acknowledge the project sponsor's request and skip the sessions.
Tell the project sponsor that skipping the sessions will jeopardize the project.
Meet with the project sponsor to understand the reasons for the time constraints.

questions.e: In this scenario, the project manager should: D. Meet with the project sponsor to understand the reasons for the time constraints. Explanation: Meeting with the project sponsor helps to understand the underlying reasons for the request to skip the focus group discussions and brainstorming sessions. This conversation can provide insights into any external pressures or constraints affecting the project timeline. It also allows the project manager to discuss the potential risks and impacts of skipping these sessions on the project's overall success, ensuring that the sponsor is fully informed of the consequences. This approach supports a collaborative decision-making process and helps in aligning project activities with the sponsor’s expectations while addressing any legitimate concerns they might have.

questions.q: A project manager is leading a project that will deliver a new product. The project manager needs to decide between options proposed by various cross-functional teams. The project manager uses a decision-making matrix and has identified criteria to evaluate the options and assign a relative weight to each criterion. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Draft a counter-proposal and share it with stakeholders.
Eliminate the alternative with the least weight.
Score each alternative for each criterion.
Choose the preferred alternative based on voting.

questions.e: After identifying criteria and assigning weights in a decision-making matrix, the project manager should: C. Score each alternative for each criterion. Explanation: Scoring each alternative involves evaluating how well each option meets the established criteria. This step allows for a systematic comparison of options based on their performance against the criteria and their relative importance (weights). By scoring each alternative, the project manager can objectively assess which option best meets the project’s needs and make an informed decision.

questions.q: The project manager for a complex project, aimed at improving the company's financial results, decides to use the Expected Monetary Value (EMV) method to select the best strategy. To achieve this, the project team defines three scenarios with the following probabilities of outcome: scenario 1 (25%), scenario 2 (50%), and scenario 3 (25%) for strategy A, with scores $160, $120, and -$20 respectively. The other strategy, strategy B, scored an EMV of $75. Which strategy will the project manager prefer? *

o.t: Strategy A with an EMV score for Strategy A of 65.
Strategy B with an EMV score for Strategy B of 75.
Strategy A with an EMV score for Strategy A of 95.
Strategy B with an EMV score for Strategy A of 95.

questions.e: To determine the preferred strategy based on Expected Monetary Value (EMV), we first need to calculate the EMV for Strategy A using the provided scenarios and probabilities. Given: Strategy A: Scenario 1: Probability = 25%, Value = $160 Scenario 2: Probability = 50%, Value = $120 Scenario 3: Probability = 25%, Value = -$20 The EMV formula is: EMV = ( Probability of Scenario 1 × Value of Scenario 1 ) + ( Probability of Scenario 2 × Value of Scenario 2 ) + ( Probability of Scenario 3 × Value of Scenario 3 ) EMV=(Probability of Scenario 1×Value of Scenario 1)+(Probability of Scenario 2×Value of Scenario 2)+(Probability of Scenario 3×Value of Scenario 3) Calculation for Strategy A: EMV = ( 0.25 × 160 ) + ( 0.50 × 120 ) + ( 0.25 × − 20 ) EMV=(0.25×160)+(0.50×120)+(0.25×−20) EMV = ( 40 ) + ( 60 ) + ( − 5 ) EMV=(40)+(60)+(−5) EMV = 95 EMV=95 Strategy B has an EMV of $75, as given. Comparison: Strategy A: EMV = $95 Strategy B: EMV = $75 Preferred Strategy: Since Strategy A has a higher EMV of $95 compared to Strategy B's EMV of $75, the project manager should prefer Strategy A. So, the correct answer is: C. Strategy A with an EMV score for Strategy A of 95.

questions.q: A project being run by a project manager is implementing a new technology. The project manager wants to be sure that the project delivers business value. What roles are critical in ensuring that the organization will benefit from the project delivery? (Choose 3). *

o.t: People and culture manager
Project manager
Business analyst
Customer lead
Technical architect

questions.e: To ensure that a project delivers business value, the following roles are critical: Project Manager (B): The project manager is essential in overseeing the project to ensure it meets its objectives, stays on schedule, and remains within budget. They are responsible for managing the project scope, risks, and ensuring that the project delivers the expected business value. Business Analyst (C): The business analyst plays a crucial role in understanding and defining the business requirements and ensuring that the project's deliverables align with those requirements. They help in translating business needs into technical specifications and ensure that the project outcomes are valuable to the organization. Customer Lead (D): The customer lead represents the interests and needs of the customer or end-user. They provide valuable input on requirements and feedback, ensuring that the project meets the expectations of the end-users and delivers value from the customer’s perspective. While roles like the technical architect (E) and people and culture manager (A) can contribute to the project's success, the project manager, business analyst, and customer lead are directly involved in ensuring the project aligns with business value and user needs. So the correct answers are: B. Project Manager C. Business Analyst D. Customer Lead

questions.q: A project manager is managing several interconnected projects. Some of these projects rely on specific deliverables from other projects. To avoid bottlenecks and facilitate project success, the project manager must assess the consolidated project plans for dependencies. What is the most appropriate action for the project manager to take in this situation? *

o.t: Identify and document all inter-project dependencies.
Adjust project timelines to remove dependencies.
Eliminate all potential inter-project dependencies.
Ensure that all projects can proceed independently.

questions.e: The most appropriate action for the project manager to take when managing interconnected projects with dependencies is: A. Identify and document all inter-project dependencies. Here’s why: Identify and document all inter-project dependencies: This is crucial for understanding how projects are linked and how delays or issues in one project might affect others. Documenting these dependencies helps in planning and managing risks effectively, ensuring that each project can align with the overall program objectives and timelines. Adjust project timelines to remove dependencies: This might not always be feasible or practical, especially if the dependencies are critical for project success. Removing dependencies could disrupt the flow and integration of the projects. Eliminate all potential inter-project dependencies: It is often unrealistic to eliminate all dependencies, especially if they are essential for the successful completion of interconnected projects. Ensure that all projects can proceed independently: If projects are highly interdependent, ensuring that they can proceed independently might not be practical and could lead to inefficiencies or incomplete deliverables. By identifying and documenting the dependencies, the project manager can better manage the schedule, resources, and risks associated with interconnected projects.

questions.q: A project manager is leading a project with numerous risks that may occur sequentially and could potentially result in significant financial consequences. What should the project manager do to better understand the risks? *

o.t: Perform a SWOT analysis with stakeholders.
Analyze a probability and impact matrix.
Participate in a brainstorming session.
Build a decision tree with the project team.

questions.e: To better understand the risks that may occur sequentially and could have significant financial consequences, the project manager should: B. Analyze a probability and impact matrix. Here’s why: Analyze a probability and impact matrix: This approach helps in evaluating and prioritizing risks based on their likelihood of occurrence and the potential impact on the project. It allows the project manager to assess which risks are most critical and need immediate attention, and which are less likely to affect the project. Perform a SWOT analysis with stakeholders: SWOT (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats) analysis is useful for identifying broad strategic issues, but it is less detailed in assessing individual risks and their potential impacts compared to a probability and impact matrix. Participate in a brainstorming session: While brainstorming is valuable for generating a list of potential risks, it does not provide the detailed analysis needed to understand their probability and impact. Build a decision tree with the project team: Decision trees are useful for evaluating different decision paths and their consequences, but they might be more complex than necessary for understanding and prioritizing risks. They are typically used once risks are identified and analyzed. Using a probability and impact matrix provides a structured way to quantify and prioritize risks, enabling better risk management and mitigation planning.

questions.q: A project manager needs to ensure that the products of the organization meet certain government standards and regulations. The project manager's team is developing a business requirements document (BRD) to help in this regard. Which of the following statements are correct about compliance requirements? (Choose 2). *

o.t: Compliance requirements are functional requirements and must be included in the BRD.
Compliance requirements are non-functional requirements and must be documented in the BRD.
Compliance requirements should be part of the project scope and should be managed by the project team.
Compliance requirements can be considered organization assets and do not need to be included in the BRD.
Compliance requirements can not be considered organization assets and must be included in the BRD.

questions.e: The correct statements about compliance requirements are: B. Compliance requirements are non-functional requirements and must be documented in the BRD. C. Compliance requirements should be part of the project scope and should be managed by the project team. Here’s why: Compliance requirements are non-functional requirements and must be documented in the BRD: Compliance requirements typically pertain to standards and regulations that affect how a product or service must perform or adhere to certain guidelines, making them non-functional requirements. They need to be documented in the Business Requirements Document (BRD) to ensure they are considered during the development process. Compliance requirements should be part of the project scope and should be managed by the project team: Compliance requirements are integral to the project’s scope, as they define the mandatory standards the project must meet. The project team is responsible for ensuring these requirements are met throughout the project.

questions.q: During a meeting, a team member on a construction project presents a proposal to the project manager. The proposal states that dividing the project into two phases will mitigate the risk of delays. The first phase would result in a minimum viable product (MVP) that would provide the client with early benefits. This would limit the extent of the damages and other cost overruns by 90%. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Conduct a feasibility study to assess the risks and benefits of the proposal.
Reject the proposal and continue with the project as initially planned.
Instruct the team to implement the proposed changes without further review.
Discuss the proposal with the client and other stakeholders to get their input.

questions.e: D. Discuss the proposal with the client and other stakeholders to get their input. Here's why: Discuss the proposal with the client and other stakeholders to get their input: Since the proposal involves changes to the project scope and delivery phases, it's crucial to involve the client and stakeholders. Their input will ensure that the revised approach aligns with their needs and expectations. This collaborative step helps validate the proposal and gain buy-in from all parties affected by the changes.

questions.q: At an agile project meeting, a team member gives an update on the status of their important task. A new team member interrupts them when they hear their task mentioned and gives a status update before the first team member has finished their update. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Privately talk to the two team members after the meeting.
Tell the new team member that they are acting unprofessionally.
Pause to discuss appropriate meeting protocol with the team.
Ask the new team member to wait until their teammate finishes.

questions.e: In this scenario, asking the new team member to wait until their teammate finishes is the most immediate and effective way to maintain meeting protocol and ensure that all team members are heard in turn. It keeps the meeting focused and respectful of everyone’s contributions, which is essential in maintaining a collaborative and efficient team environment.

questions.q: A multi-year project is underway when a key resource announces that they are retiring. The project manager is concerned about the impact on the project and has identified that several critical tasks will be affected. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Require the remaining team members to work additional hours to complete the impacted tasks.
Advise the stakeholders that the resource's tasks will not be completed on time.
Collaborate with the resource manager to identify and train an appropriate replacement.
Encourage the retiring team member to postpone retirement to avoid disrupting the project.

questions.e: The most appropriate action for the project manager in this situation is: C. Collaborate with the resource manager to identify and train an appropriate replacement. Here’s why: Proactive Approach: Working with the resource manager to find and train a replacement helps ensure a smooth transition and continuity of work, minimizing disruptions to the project. Long-Term Solution: This approach addresses the root of the problem by preparing a new team member to take over the critical tasks, rather than just managing the immediate impact. Stakeholder Communication: While it's important to keep stakeholders informed, this option does not address the underlying issue of finding a replacement and preparing them for the role.

questions.q: A project manager must make decisions daily, regardless of the decision's level of importance or criticality. What should a project manager do to ensure their decisions are unbiased and rational? *

o.t: Utilize data without checking for accuracy
Understand they cannot achieve everything
Make decisions quickly
Make decisions only when the results are certain

questions.e: To ensure decisions are unbiased and rational, a project manager should: B. Understand they cannot achieve everything Here's why: Realistic Expectations: Recognizing that it is impossible to achieve everything helps a project manager prioritize tasks and make decisions that align with project goals and constraints, ensuring they are based on practical and achievable objectives. Balanced Decision-Making: By understanding limitations, the project manager can focus on making informed decisions within the scope of what is feasible, considering available resources and constraints.

questions.q: A project manager is assigned to a top innovation project that has high visibility with the company executives. Recently, one of the project requirements changed and requires the use of new and innovative technology. The change requires the creation of a new position to be filled by someone familiar with the new technology. During a status meeting, a current team member expresses interest in the new role and confirms they are certified in this new technology. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Reassign the team member to the task to support their growth at the organization, and acquire a resource to replace the team member's old role.
Ask the team member to continue the current job assignment while also taking on the new assignment as time allows.
Escalate the request to the project sponsor in order to determine if the team member can be assigned to the new assignment.
Hire a new team member and ask the existing team member to provide the training needed for the new team member to obtain certification.

questions.e: Given the scenario, the most appropriate action for the project manager is: A. Reassign the team member to the task to support their growth at the organization, and acquire a resource to replace the team member's old role. Here's why: Supporting Growth: Reassigning the team member to the new role aligns with their interest and expertise, supporting their professional development and contributing to the project's success. Minimizing Disruption: By acquiring a resource to replace the team member's old role, the project manager ensures that the existing tasks are still covered, preventing disruption in the project's progress.

questions.q: A project manager is managing a project with a hybrid approach and has requested a senior team member to perform a quantitative risk analysis. The team member responds that they do not have the knowledge to perform such an analysis. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Escalate the issue to the functional manager.
Contact the project management office (PMO) and request them to assign another team member who has the knowledge to perform this task to the team.
Help the team member to perform the quantitative risk analysis through coaching, mentoring, and training.
Perform the quantitative risk analysis for the team member.

questions.e: Given the situation, the best course of action for the project manager is: C. Help the team member to perform the quantitative risk analysis through coaching, mentoring, and training. Here's why: Skill Development: Helping the team member through coaching, mentoring, and training builds their skills, which is beneficial for both the current project and future projects. Team Empowerment: By investing in the team member’s growth, the project manager fosters a more capable and resilient team. Immediate Needs: It addresses the immediate need for performing the quantitative risk analysis while also enhancing the team member’s skill set for future tasks.

questions.q: A new member joined a project during the execution phase. The work requires strong collaboration with other team members. What should the project manager do to foster a collaborative environment? *

o.t: Send an email to the project team asking them to collaborate with the new team member.
Share all information available and allocate time to explain in detail the work in progress.
Ask each member to describe their interests and experience in the next team meeting.
Organize a one-day workshop with the entire team to bring the new member up to speed.

questions.e: Option D—Organize a one-day workshop with the entire team to bring the new member up to speed—is the best approach for several reasons: Comprehensive Introduction: A workshop provides a structured environment where the new team member can be introduced to all aspects of the project, including its goals, current progress, and key deliverables. This helps them understand the project's context and their role within it. Facilitates Team Integration: By bringing the entire team together, the workshop allows for personal introductions and helps build relationships. This is crucial for fostering a collaborative environment and ensuring that the new member feels welcomed and included. Encourages Open Communication: The workshop setting encourages open dialogue, where team members can discuss ongoing work, clarify any doubts, and share insights. This helps the new member get up to speed quickly and align their work with the team's objectives.
